interpretation: On the 9 tests that were run for both versions (T01–T09), the biggest improvement came from v1 to v3: passes rose from 0/9 to 9/9, solution leaks fell from 9/9 to 0/9, and v3 returned valid JSON in 9/9 runs and correctly reported `no_issues` for the clean code in T09, where v1 rewrote the function anyway. v2, tests T10–T16 and the full v4 chain (P1 + P2 Hint Guard) could not be run because the free-tier daily quota (20 requests per model) ran out; only v4's input validator was checked (T14, rejected with 0 API calls). All runs used `gemini-3.5-flash`, because `gemini-2.5-flash`, named in the prompt-file headers, returns 404 for new API keys.
metrics_note: All numbers come from real API calls saved in `test-data/results/` (model `gemini-3.5-flash`; `gemini-2.5-flash`, named in the prompt-file headers, now returns 404 for new API keys). The free-tier quota of 20 requests per model per day ran out during the run, so each fraction is over the tests that were actually run: v1 and v3 on T01–T09, v4 on T14 only, and v2 not run.
test_table_note: Before the API quota ran out, v4 could only be run on T14. For T01–T09 the table shows the v3 run, which uses the same P1 prompt text and settings as v4 but without the validator, schema retry and Hint Guard; these rows are marked *(v3 run)*. T10–T13, T15 and T16 were not run.

screenshot_note: Screenshots of v4 runs on T01, T10 and T12 could not be taken because each needs two model calls and the API quota was used up. They will be added after the full re-run.

limitations.title: Evaluation is incomplete.
limitations.text: The free-tier Gemini key allows 20 requests per model per day, and it ran out after 19 test runs. So v2, tests T10–T16 and the full v4 chain were not evaluated, and the P2 Hint Guard has no measured result yet.
limitations.short: Free-tier quota (20 requests per model per day) ran out, so v2, T10–T16 and the v4 chain with P2 are not yet evaluated.

limitations.title: The deployed app shares the same quota.
limitations.text: Each v4 review uses 2 model calls, so a free-tier key supports about 10 reviews a day. After that the app shows a 429 quota error.
limitations.short: Each v4 review uses 2 calls, so the free tier allows about 10 reviews a day; after that the app shows a quota error.
limitations.next: Move the key to a paid tier, show a friendly "daily limit reached" message, and skip P2 when a cheap local check finds no code-like text in the hints.

limitations.title: The leak check is rule-based.
limitations.text: Our automatic test only catches fixes that match known snippets or code blocks, so a fix fully described in words could pass. It also needed one correction during testing: a block of printed program output (`1 False`) in v1 T09 was first counted as code, so a block now counts only if it contains a Python statement. (T09 is still counted as a leak because v1 also rewrote the whole function.)
limitations.short: The leak check matches known fix snippets and code blocks, so a fix fully described in words could pass.
limitations.next: Add an LLM-as-judge leak check with a rubric and compare it with a human check on 10 outputs.

limitations.title: Python only, short programs.
limitations.text: Other languages are rejected and programs over 150 lines are refused.
limitations.short: Only Python programs of up to 150 lines are supported.
limitations.next: Test C support with a separate few-shot set.
